conceptBreakdown.content:
An **Electrocardiogram (ECG)** is the graphic recording of the electrical potential changes generated by the cardiac conducting system during the cardiac cycle, recorded using standard limb leads (**Einthoven’s Triangle**).

### 7.1 ECG Waveform Component Matrix

| ECG Deflection / Segment | Electrophysiological Cardiac Event | Clinical / Diagnostic Significance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **P Wave** | **Atrial Depolarization** (spreading from SA node across both atria) | Precedes atrial contraction; absent or inverted in atrial fibrillation/SA block |
| **QRS Complex** | **Ventricular Depolarization** (rapid spread through Bundle of His / Purkinje fibers) | Triggers ventricular contraction. **Counting QRS complexes per minute determines Heart Rate!** |
| **T Wave** | **Ventricular Repolarization** (return of ventricles from excited to resting state) | Marks the end of ventricular systole |
| **P-R Interval** | Time taken for excitation to travel from SA node through AV node to ventricles | Prolonged in **First-Degree AV Block** ($>0.20\text{ s}$) |
| **S-T Segment** | Period when entire ventricular myocardium is fully depolarized | **ST Elevation** indicates acute **Myocardial Infarction**; ST depression indicates Ischemia |
